summary: Obfuscated preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated sibling bundle under it
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is heavily obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style _0x-prefixed identifiers, wrapper-object property proxies) and, on npm install, downloads a Bun runtime archive for the host platform and architecture from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods the binary executable, and invokes it with the sibling file math_init.js as its argument. math_init.js is a 727 KB single-line bundle protected by a shuffled string-array plus rotator function (WV8StW pushes/shifts the array), rendering it non-auditable in shipped form. Executing an obfuscated bundle under an alternate language runtime pulled at preinstall time gives the publisher arbitrary code execution on every installing machine and evades Node-based static and dynamic analysis. The Bun download itself is from Bun's official GitHub release host, but the delivery vehicle for the code that actually runs is the shipped obfuscated math_init.js — a deployments SDK has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime at preinstall and hand it an opaque sibling file.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
